newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura gives Kety buy rating.
newsitem.headline: Nomura gives Kety buy rating.

text.p: Investors should buy shares in the Polish Kety aluminium plant, bolstered by funds gained from the share issue that accompanied the firm's bourse flotation at the turn of the year, Nomura Equity Research said.
"Kety has the balance-sheet strength to modernise all divisions and consider expansion into new areas of business," Nomura said in a report dated September 2.
Since then Kety, whose full name is Zaklady Metali Lekkich Kety SA, has risen to 191 from 189 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse.

Nomura said that though the recent fall in aluminium prices will cause a drop in reported sales for 1996, especially in its casting alloys division, its extruded products and packaging divisions were less exposed.

It said Kety should also benefit in 1997 from its "exciting new equipment" including a new production line that processes scrap aluminium cans, and from 1998 by increased demand in the car production industry.
Nomura predicted Kety would lift pre-tax earnings to 45 million zlotys this year and to 60 million zlotys in 1997. The company's pre-tax profit was at 40.5 million zlotys last year.
It said the firm's price-earnings ratio, currently at 22.5, should shrink to 15.4 based on 1996 earnings and 11.5 based on 1997 earnings.
